newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Farm Min sees '97 grain output at 24 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Polish Farm Min sees '97 grain output at 24 mln T.

text.p: Poland's Agriculture Ministry said on Friday that according to its preliminary estimates grain output should fall to around 24 million tonnes in 1997 from 25.3 million in 1996.
The ministry estimates this year's rapeseed output at around 550,000 tonnes, up from last year's 461,000 tonnes, its spokeswoman Malgorzata Ksiazek told Reuters.
"According to very preliminary Agriculture Ministry estimates the rapeseed harvest is expected to be around 550,000 tonnes and grain harvest around 24 million tonnes," she said.
Ksiazek added that Agriculture Minister Jaroslaw Kalinowski said in a Friday radio interview that Poland's grain harvest could even fall below 24 million, but did not elaborate.
She said the quality of this year's grain varied according to the region in which it was grown and that Poland would again import high-quality wheat, not grown domestically, in the 1997/98 season.
